dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering

evidence.note: Before writing code, read helpers.py, run.sh, conftest.py, and all ~14 test_*_public.py files (api/engine/spill/deps/copy_fill/sort_filter/csv/collab/xlsx/ooxml/iter/pivot/locale/validation) — comprehensive extraction of the entire client-exercised contract surface, stronger than a level-5 'reads helpers.py and run.sh'.

Deliberate library evaluation: installed and probed the `formulas` library, confirmed 645 functions incl. dynamic-array (BYCOL/BYROW/FILTER/SORT), explicitly stated intent to 'verify capabilities for Excel-365 functions... and check if it supports spill' — genuine feature-support verification of a chosen library.

Continued probing formulas library's ExcelModel vs get_functions() approaches, tested SUM/VLOOKUP callable, discovered ExcelModel is file-based and pivoted engine strategy — deliberate OOXML/eval library selection grounded in observed behavior.

After the initial reading, the entire remaining trajectory is consumed by heredoc-escaping and deadlock debugging; no durable contract-map artifact is built and the client/tests are never re-consulted as new subsystems are reached — falls short of level 8/10's explicit reference and contract-driven-throughout behavior.

Excel-semantics for tricky areas (spill, #CIRC!, iterative calc, locale) are enumerated as requirements but grounded in the test files rather than independently probed against Excel/LibreOffice ground truth — the level-8 'probes Excel semantics rather than assuming' bar is only partially met.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent thoroughly read the full client-exercised contract surface (helpers.py, run.sh, conftest, and every public test file) upfront and made deliberate, verified library choices (formulas lib capability-checked, openpyxl for OOXML), which exceeds the level-5 'working model' anchor. But it never distilled this into an explicit cross-referenced reference map, its Excel-semantics grounding for the hard areas was inferred from tests rather than independently probed, and it never re-consulted the contract as subsystems were reached (implementation stalled in escaping/deadlock issues). That places it between the level-5 and level-8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones

evidence.note: Read all dev_test files to grasp full scope, then stated a flat enumeration of subsystems (persistence, engine, REST, WebSocket, SPA) with no dependency ordering or per-item done-check.
Expressed genuine dependency-aware phasing intent: 'Start with a basic FastAPI server, then add formula engine, persistence, and all endpoints' — a rough skeleton→engine→extras staging.
Concrete checkpoint intent: build a minimal server that passes the health check first, then iteratively add features — the one clear stage-checkpoint tied to behavior.

Plan degenerates into a static repeated debugging loop (kill/fix/restart/test/run-suite) reprinted dozens of times; no milestone hierarchy, no per-layer done-criteria, no re-ordering as understanding deepened.

Final steps still stuck on the same deadlock fix with the same 5-step loop; the surface was never decomposed into sequenced, individually-verifiable milestones beyond 'get health green then everything else.'

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went beyond a purely flat to-do list (anchor 3) by voicing dependency-aware phasing — contract reading → health skeleton → engine → endpoints — with a health-endpoint checkpoint, which touches anchor 5's 'sensible stages with rough checkpoints.' But that phasing stayed aspirational: there were no concrete per-milestone done-checks tied to runnable tests, high-risk load-bearing layers (spill/recompute/graph) were never front-loaded, and the plan never evolved — it collapsed into a static, repeated deadlock-debugging loop for the back half of the trajectory. That places it between the flat-list and sensible-phasing anchors, at a 4.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite

evidence.note: Tested the `formulas` library directly against a known value (SUM=10.0, VLOOKUP) — a small oracle-grounding of a candidate library, the closest thing to an expected-value check, but of a dependency, not its own engine.
Repeatedly attempted to run dev_tests/run.sh throughout the trajectory as the primary verification signal, but never achieved more than the health endpoint passing (11 endpoints timed out).
Manual curl probes of create/patch/GET endpoints — but these are liveness/smoke checks of whether endpoints respond, not comparisons of formula outputs against expected Excel results.

Read the smoke-suite files to learn the contract, but never converted that into self-built probes for spill, error sentinels, xlsx round-trip, performance bounds, collab, locale, iterative calc, or goal-seek — none of those subsystems were independently verified.
The entire final third is consumed debugging a deadlock and terminal buffering; no verification harness beyond the provided smoke suite is ever constructed, and the run never goes green.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran the provided smoke suite regularly and did manual curl endpoint probing plus one small library-level oracle check (SUM=10.0), which places it above anchor 3's 'run.sh occasionally.' But its manual checks were largely liveness probes rather than genuine formula-vs-Excel value comparisons, and it built nothing beyond the smoke suite — no error-sentinel, spill, xlsx-round-trip, or performance probes (anchor 8 is entirely absent). It lands at 4: between reliance on the smoke suite and true hand-checking against Excel values.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface

evidence.note: Formed only a coarse mental inventory of major subsystems (engine, REST, WebSocket, XLSX/CSV, SPA, 'many features'); repeated verbatim across steps. No granular per-function/endpoint ledger of the ~150-function catalog.
Enumerated subsystems as a numbered list (1) persistence (2) formula eval (3) REST (4) WebSocket (5) SPA — a coarse checklist, but never maintained/updated as areas were verified complete.

Circular debugging: the identical 'Lock non-reentrant deadlock + regex escaping' diagnosis is restated in dozens of consecutive Analysis blocks with the same kill/sed/restart/test cycle. The agent never detects it is looping or changes tactics — the exact failure mode anchor 8 penalizes.
Submitted 'task complete' while still stuck in the deadlock loop (only health test passing), then continued looping to step 253 — showing no accurate live picture reconciled against verification.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept only a vague, prose-based awareness of major feature families (never lost whole areas, and had a coarse numbered subsystem list), which lifts it above the 0-2 band. But it never maintained a granular done/partial/not-started ledger, and — decisively for this dimension — it failed catastrophically at detecting stuck/circular states, restating an identical diagnosis and re-running the same fix cycle for ~90 steps without noticing the loop or adjusting. That places it at the 'vague mental tracking, no reliable stuck-detection' level (3), well below the maintained-checklist (5) and self-correcting-ledger (8) anchors.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions

evidence.note: Genuine design-level adaptation: tried formulas.ExcelModel, found it is file-based and doesn't fit a cell-referenced model, and pivoted to a custom engine reusing get_functions() implementations. A real course-correction on a falsified library assumption.

Correctly diagnosed the root cause of all-endpoints-timeout as a non-reentrant threading.Lock deadlock (patch_cells holds wb_lock then save_state re-acquires) plus a \\d+ regex-escaping bug. Root-cause identification of a falsified assumption, but it's a concurrency/tooling crash, not an Excel/spill/recompute semantic assumption.

For ~150 steps the agent repeats the identical Lock->RLock + regex patch, restarts, re-runs tests, but never confirms the fix landed or achieves green — near-verbatim repeated analysis. Failure to detect that its correction approach itself is not progressing; no re-verification loop closes.

Server reached 2558 lines with full engine/endpoints, but the trajectory never advanced past the deadlock to exercise Excel edge cases, spill, topological order, or perf budgets — so no adaptation on the semantic assumptions the dimension targets ever occurred.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent shows one authentic early design pivot (ExcelModel to custom engine) and a correct root-cause diagnosis of a deadlock, which lifts it above 'ignores contradicting evidence.' But the dominant, whole-horizon behavior matches anchor 3: it reacts to a hard crash with a local patch (RLock/regex) and never revisits or re-verifies, getting trapped in a ~150-step non-progressing loop that repeats the same fix. It never reached the Excel/spill/recompute/perf assumptions this dimension centers on, so there is no evidence of reworking a semantic design (anchor 8) — placing it at 3.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort

evidence.note: Explicitly chose to reuse the `formulas` library's 645 built-in function implementations rather than hand-write the catalog ('save enormous time/effort') — a genuine breadth-securing allocation decision that trades depth for broad function coverage cheaply.

Read every dev_test contract file to size the full surface before building; shows scope awareness but the resulting plans are all undifferentiated 'build all endpoints/all features' with no graded-return prioritization or niche deferral.

Plans order work core-engine-then-endpoints by dependency default, not by conscious high-value-first triage; intent is 'covering all features' / 'passes all visible tests' — breadth without allocation strategy.

Remainder consumed by heredoc-escaping and an unresolved deadlock (1 pass/11 timeouts); never reached feature-level implementation, so no reallocation as verification revealed marginal yield — the coverage-triage horizon was never exercised.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent made one real triage act — reusing a library to secure broad function coverage cheaply — and sized the full surface up front, which lifts it above the arbitrary-order anchor (3). But it never articulated graded-return reasoning, never consciously deferred or timeboxed low-yield niches, and its plans were uniformly 'build everything'; the core-first ordering was a dependency default rather than value-based prioritization. That places it between arbitrary implementation (3) and deliberate high-value-first prioritization (5), i.e. a 4.

rubric.task_read: This is an extremely long-horizon, high-complexity build: a full Excel-clone product (persistent HTTP server + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a formula engine spanning ~150 functions, Excel-365 dynamic arrays/spill, a dependency graph with performance-bounded dirty recompute, xlsx/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (defined names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek, iterative calc). The exact wire contract is under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client, and grading is on a much larger HIDDEN suite plus value-by-value comparison against a LibreOffice oracle. This task demands maximal, sustained meta-work across all five faculties: deep upfront orientation on the contract, aggressive decomposition/sequencing of an enormous surface, self-built verification well beyond the smoke suite, tight progress tracking, and constant course-correction as Excel edge cases falsify assumptions.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reverse-engineering
dimensions.description: Extracting the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and the smoke suite, and grounding formula/feature behavior in Excel/LibreOffice semantics, before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire shapes are defined ONLY by what the first-party client calls, and grading compares values against a LibreOffice oracle. Guessing shapes or semantics guarantees hidden-suite failures no matter how good the code is; this is the single highest-leverage meta-activity here.

anchors.0: Starts writing the server/engine without reading helpers.py or dev_tests; invents endpoint and cell shapes from imagination.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once; picks up a few obvious shapes but leaves most of the contract (patch/fill/sort/spill/collab payloads, kind discriminator, envelope) inferred loosely.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and run.sh to extract the concrete request/response shapes it exercises, chooses libraries (OOXML I/O, formula eval) deliberately, and forms a working model of the core cell/formula contract.
anchors.8: Systematically maps every endpoint, discriminator, and payload the client touches into an explicit reference; probes Excel semantics for genuinely tricky areas (spill ghosts, #SPILL!/#CIRC!, iterative fixed-point, locale canonicalization, xlsx openpyxl round-trip) rather than assuming; verifies chosen libraries actually support required features (CF, styles, named ranges).
anchors.10: Builds a durable, cross-referenced contract map reconciling helpers.py, the smoke suite, and Excel/LibreOffice ground truth; proactively surfaces ambiguities and resolves them from observed client behavior; re-consults the client/oracle as new subsystems are reached, so implementation is contract-driven throughout rather than only at the start.

dimensions.name: Sequencing the feature surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking an enormous, interdependent surface into an ordered hierarchy of sub-goals — each with an explicit done-check — sequenced by dependency and risk.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are dozens of endpoint families and ~150 functions with hard dependencies (health/persistence → contract → engine → graph → dynamic arrays → analyst surface → collab/xlsx). Without deliberate ordering and done-criteria, the agent cannot sustain progress or know when a layer is solid enough to build on.

anchors.0: Treats the whole product as one undifferentiated push; jumps between unrelated features with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat, one-time to-do list of features with no dependency ordering and no per-item way to know it's done.
anchors.5: Phases the work into sensible stages (skeleton/health first, then engine, then extras) with rough checkpoints per stage.
anchors.8: An explicit milestone hierarchy sequenced by dependency and risk (get a live server + persistence + contract-correct core cell round-trip green before breadth), each milestone with a concrete done-check tied to a runnable test.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone plan that front-loads the highest-risk load-bearing layers (dependency graph, spill, recompute correctness/performance), defines done-criteria in terms of verifiable behavior, and is revisited and re-ordered as scope understanding deepens — never a static checklist.

dimensions.name: Self-built verification beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately constructing checks — formula-value oracles, round-trip tests, error-sentinel and performance probes — rather than trusting the non-exhaustive smoke suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly warns the visible suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a much larger hidden suite plus cell-by-cell comparison to LibreOffice. An agent that only runs run.sh is flying blind on the majority of what's graded.

anchors.0: No verification; assumes code works, or never runs the provided smoke suite.
anchors.3: Runs dev_tests/run.sh occasionally and treats a green smoke run as done.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite regularly and hand-checks a few formulas/endpoints against expected Excel values.
anchors.8: Builds its own targeted tests well beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking function outputs against known Excel results, exercising error sentinels, spill collisions, xlsx round-trip via openpyxl, and the stated performance bounds — using failures to drive fixes.
anchors.10: Stands up a systematic verification harness covering breadth of the catalog and subsystems (dynamic arrays, collab seq/broadcast, locale, iterative calc, goal-seek convergence, xlsx fidelity), grounds expected values in an Excel/LibreOffice oracle, benchmarks the performance ceilings, and treats verification as the primary signal steering what to build/fix next.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions, endpoints, and subsystems are complete vs outstanding, and detecting stuck/circular states.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~150 functions and ~15 feature families over a very long horizon, it is easy to lose the plot, double-implement, or silently drop whole categories; sustained accurate tracking is what prevents both gaps and thrash.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done or left; forgets whole feature areas or repeatedly reworks the same thing without noticing.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; periodically rediscovers unfinished areas by accident.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of major features and updates it as areas are completed.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular ledger of the function catalog and endpoint families (done / partial / not-started), and notices when it is stuck or re-debugging the same issue, adjusting rather than looping.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate running picture across the entire surface for the whole horizon, reconciled against verification results (not just self-report), promptly detects thrashing/circular debugging or a stalled subsystem, and reallocates effort deliberately in response.

dimensions.name: Course-correcting on falsified Excel/perf assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality — Excel edge cases, spill/recompute behavior, performance limits, contract mismatches — diverges from expectations.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Excel semantics and the dependency/spill/iterative machinery are riddled with edge cases; initial designs (e.g. naive recompute, spill handling, locale parsing) will be falsified. Barrelling ahead on a wrong assumption compounds into wide test failures.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps pushing a falsified design (e.g. recompute that misses dependents or blows the perf budget) unchanged.
anchors.3: Reacts only to hard crashes with local patches; doesn't revisit the underlying approach when results are subtly wrong.
anchors.5: Fixes issues as tests surface them and makes reasonable local design changes when something clearly doesn't work.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a wrong assumption (dependency-graph model, spill materialization, topological order, contract shape) and reworks the relevant design rather than piling on patches.
anchors.10: Detects divergence early from verification signals, diagnoses the root assumption, revises the affected design deliberately, and re-verifies — repeatedly steering the build back on course without derailing unaffected subsystems.

dimensions.name: Coverage allocation under finite effort
dimensions.description: Deciding which of the vast feature/function set to build (and in what breadth-vs-depth balance) to maximize graded coverage on the hidden suite given limited time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is far larger than can be perfected; graded return is maximized by consciously trading breadth of working features against depth on a few. This allocation decision is distinct from ordering milestones — it's about what NOT to over-invest in and where partial coverage still scores.

anchors.0: No triage: rabbit-holes on one function/feature (e.g. perfecting one distribution) while leaving whole graded areas unimplemented.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no regard to graded return; over-polishes some corners while omitting entire common families.
anchors.5: Roughly prioritizes high-frequency, high-value features (core math/lookup/text, cell round-trip) before niche ones.
anchors.8: Explicitly reasons about graded return — securing broad working coverage of common functions and endpoints before deep edge-case work, and consciously deferring or timeboxing low-yield niches.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, revisited allocation strategy: breadth-first correctness across the catalog and endpoint families, timeboxed depth on high-risk/high-value areas, and reallocation as verification reveals where marginal effort buys the most hidden-suite coverage.
